description: This bar chart illustrates the sample counts for essay types categorized as Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository, with a distinction between “Open” and “Cons.” (Constrained) sets. The horizontal axis represents the essay type categories with labels in the order Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository. The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 120, with tick marks at 20-unit intervals. Each essay type is represented by two bars grouped side-by-side: a light blue bar representing the “Open” set and a light red bar representing the “Cons.” set. For Argumentative essays, the “Open” bar reaches a value of 79, while the “Cons.” bar reaches 122. For Narrative essays, the “Open” bar reaches 80, and the “Cons.” bar reaches 130. The “Open” bar for Descriptive essays extends to 68, with the “Cons.” bar extending to 100. Finally, the “Open” bar for Expository essays reaches a value of 62, and the “Cons.” bar reaches 122. The bars are arranged in order of the essay type categories, without any apparent sorting within the groupings. Each bar displays its exact numeric value above its top edge, and no bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
